analysis.title: Equity Correlation Rises / Bull Market Intact / SPX Capitulation Signals
key_insights: Zain Nizami (Cash Equity Voice Trading) says the US equity story has moved from sector rotation to correlation: index-level moves now sit on top of the rotations already underway. If correlation keeps rising, the sell-off spreads from crowded sectors and relative-value positions into broader portfolio risk.

Nizami sees support for rest-of-world versus US equities after the political shift, via potentially lower oil. He says the 'Trump put' helps RoW through lower oil more than it helps Tech, which had led US outperformance.
Nizami says positioning matters more than fundamentals right now. Memory fell 16% on Thursday but is still up 78% on the year.

Unlike the July sell-off, long-only accounts have not yet stepped in as buyers. In July, long-only accounts, CTAs and retail absorbed the deleveraging. The desk sees no equivalent demand yet, even though leverage is cleaner than in July.

Jason Perl (UBS Knowledge Network): technicals point to a corrective sell-off, not the end of the bull market. He sees risk/reward skewed higher into year-end and an eventual SPX target of 8,485 next year.

Perl: SOX hit both its daily and weekly TD Propulsion downside targets on Thursday. 63.3% of constituents are at or near DeMark Buy signals, and a TD Combo 13 Buy could trigger as soon as Monday. SOX recovery levels are 9,264 and 9,530, and 9,938 would relieve the immediate downside threat. NDX is about one day behind.

Rebecca Cheong (Derivatives Strategist) expects SPX to set a low on Monday. Three capitulation signals have triggered: excess sell flow of $365 bn (a record), UBS RMM flow buying the dip at the 68th percentile after the largest selling episode since covid, and a VIX Cross-Asset Rank of 96%.

Cheong: systematic strategies sold an estimated $170-210 bn Thursday (Risk Control $95-125 bn, Leveraged ETFs $50-55 bn, CTA $25-30 bn). Risk Control could sell another $200-270 bn over the next two days. After Monday, Risk Control and CTA rebalancing flows are expected to become very small.
Cheong: Thursday investor conversations were not shocked, and there was substantial interest in deploying capital into weakness rather than broad capitulation.

UBS industrials analyst Amit Mehrota thinks the market is conflating data centre regulation with a halt. The AI-exposed industrials sell-off followed the Democratic midterm sweep, including governors in Texas and Georgia who have advocated moratoriums on new data centre approvals. He sees the policy debate focusing on self-reliance in power, grid and water, which affects suppliers of electrical and thermal infrastructure differently.

US payrolls preview: economist Jonathan Pingle raised his October NFP forecast to 75K, with private payrolls up 75K and government flat. Initial claims fell 6K to 189K, but a New York unemployment-insurance outage should depress claims for two weeks and then cause a catch-up rebound. Q3 productivity rose 3.6% annualized and unit labour costs fell 0.7% annualized (+2.4% y/y).

Banxico unexpectedly cut 25bp to 6.25% in a 3-2 vote against expectations for a hold, calling it a 'one-off adjustment' and guiding to a 'prolonged period' at the new level. UBS reads it as a recalibration, not the start of a cutting cycle. USDMXN hit 18.95 and was 18.82 afterward.

German September industrial production rose 0.7% m/m (consensus -0.1%) and 0.4% y/y (forecast +1.2%). Factory orders rose 4.4% m/m and October manufacturing PMI was 54.2. September retail sales fell 2.0% m/m against a consensus of +0.4%.

About 575,000 people protested in France on Thursday, the largest since September. The National Assembly rejected the 2027 budget revenue measures 458-0, and a Senate vote is expected Dec. 9. The government could use Article 49.3, ordinances after Dec. 17, or a special law rolling over 2026 levels.

New Zealand votes Saturday. Labour leads National 30.7% to 26.4% in the Post/Freshwater poll, and Opportunity is at 5.1%, just above the 5% threshold. A National-led coalition could give the RBNZ room for gradual OCR hikes. A Labour-led coalition would restore the dual mandate and raise spending and taxes.

Japan September average cash earnings rose 4.6% y/y, the fastest since January 1997, and real wages rose 2.2% y/y. This supports further BoJ hikes, with the market expecting the next move in December.

GPIF lost 1.7% in the three months to September. Its 25% allocation to each of four asset buckets is unchanged, so there is no sign of imminent JPY repatriation. Near-term JPY support comes from safe-haven demand and narrower rate differentials as US AI slowdown concerns lower Fed hike pricing.

PM Takaichi wants to reinvest the proceeds of the BoJ's accelerated ETF sales into economic-security sectors. The BoJ plans to raise annual ETF sales to JPY860 bn from JPY330 bn starting in January. Funding for defense spending and a food sales tax cut faces a year-end deadline.

ETD Rates: the 2-5Y Treasury sector caught a safety bid. A December Fed hike is priced at 66%, down from 81% Wednesday. Flows included 50k Week 1 TY 107.50/108 call spreads bought for 10, a block buyer of 8,200 TUZ6, and 35k SFRZ6 95.9375/96.0625/96.1875 call flies. The desk expects more Fed-on-hold plays if equity moves continue.

FX: the tech sell-off is a classic risk-off pattern, with USD firmer and CHF and JPY supported. Commodity currencies are weakest. EURUSD support is at 1.1180, then 1.1100/10, and resistance is at 1.1215/20 and 1.1260/70.

tension_points.bull_case: Technicals say the sell-off is corrective. Three capitulation signals triggered, the derivatives desk expects an SPX low Monday, and UBS keeps an eventual 8,485 SPX target next year.
tension_points.bear_case: Correlation is rising so the pain spreads into broader portfolio risk, and long-only buyers who defended the July sell-off have not appeared.
tension_points.what_invalidates: SOX holding below its recent lows with no recovery toward 9,264 and 9,530, and no long-only dip buying emerging after systematic selling fades after Monday.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising correlation moves the pain from crowded sectors into broader portfolio risk, and long-only buyers are absent so far.
theme_stances.evidence: Correlation is picking up and, if that continues, the sell-off becomes much harder to hide from.

theme_stances.key_argument: Three capitulation signals suggest forced selling and oversold conditions, with an SPX low possible Monday.
theme_stances.evidence: My expectation is that SPX could establish a low on Monday
